{{Short description|PDE to describe nonlinear wave motion}}
[[File:Ile de ré.JPG|thumb|right|300px|Crossing [[swell (ocean)|swell]]s, consisting of near-cnoidal wave trains. Photo taken from Phares des Baleines (Whale Lighthouse) at the western point of [[Île de Ré]] (Isle of Rhé), France, in the [[Atlantic Ocean]]. The interaction of such near-[[soliton]]s in shallow water may be modeled through the Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation.]]
In [[mathematics]] and [[physics]], the '''Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation''' (often abbreviated as '''KP equation''') is a [[partial differential equation]] to describe [[nonlinear]] [[wave motion]]. Named after [[Boris Kadomtsev|Boris Borisovich Kadomtsev]] and [[Vladimir Iosifovich Petviashvili]], the KP equation is usually written as
<math display=block>\displaystyle \partial_x(\partial_t u+u \partial_x u+\epsilon^2\partial_{xxx}u)+\lambda\partial_{yy}u=0</math>
where <math>\lambda=\pm 1</math>.  The above form shows that the KP equation is a generalization to two [[spatial dimension]]s, ''x'' and ''y'', of the one-dimensional [[Korteweg–de Vries equation|Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation]]. To be physically meaningful, the wave propagation direction has to be not-too-far from the ''x'' direction, i.e. with only slow variations of solutions in the ''y'' direction. The transverse stability and dynamics of a single planar soliton with respect to finite-amplitude and wavelength perturbations are described by the [[Shrira-Pesenson equation]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Shrira |first1=V. I. |last2=Pesenson |first2=M. Z. |year=1984 |title=Soliton stability with respect to transverse perturbations of finite length and amplitude |journal=Nonlinear and Turbulent Processes in Physics |page=1061 |bibcode=1984ntpp.proc.1061S}}</ref>

Like the KdV equation, the KP equation is completely integrable.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cheng |first1=Y. |last2=Li |first2=Y. S. |year=1991 |title=The constraint of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation and its special solutions |journal=Physics Letters A |volume=157 |issue=1 |pages=22–26 |doi=10.1016/0375-9601(91)90403-U |bibcode=1991PhLA..157...22C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Ma |first=W. X. |year=2015 |title=Lump solutions to the Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation |journal=Physics Letters A |volume=379 |issue=36 |pages=1975–1978 |doi=10.1016/j.physleta.2015.06.061 |bibcode=2015PhLA..379.1975M }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Kodama |first=Y. |year=2004 |title=Young diagrams and N-soliton solutions of the KP equation |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General |volume=37 |issue=46 |pages=11169–11190 |doi=10.1088/0305-4470/37/46/006 |arxiv=nlin/0406033 |bibcode=2004JPhA...3711169K |s2cid=2071043 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Deng |first1=S. F. |last2=Chen |first2=D. Y. |last3=Zhang |first3=D. J. |year=2003 |title=The multisoliton solutions of the KP equation with self-consistent sources |journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan |volume=72 |issue=9 |pages=2184–2192 |doi=10.1143/JPSJ.72.2184 |bibcode=2003JPSJ...72.2184D }}</ref> It can also be solved using the [[inverse scattering transform]] much like the [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ablowitz |first1=M. J. |last2=Segur |first2=H. |year=1981 |title=Solitons and the inverse scattering transform |publisher=SIAM }}</ref>

The [[Lax pair]] representation for the KP equation, which underlies its integrability by the inverse scattering transform, was first obtained by Valery Dryuma in 1974,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Dryuma |first=V. S. |year=1974 |title=Analytic solution of the two-dimensional Korteweg–de Vries (KdV) equation |journal=Soviet Physics JETP Letters |volume=19 |pages=753–757}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Biondini |first1=G. |last2=Pelinovsky |first2=D. |year=2008 |title=Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation |journal=[[Scholarpedia]] |volume=3 |issue=10 |page=6539 |doi=10.4249/scholarpedia.6539 |doi-access=free}}</ref> shortly before the inverse scattering method for two-dimensional equations was developed by [[Vladimir E. Zakharov|Zakharov]] and [[Alexei Borisovich Shabat|Shabat]] the same year.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zakharov |first1=V. E. |last2=Shabat |first2=A. B. |year=1974 |title=A scheme for integrating the nonlinear equations of mathematical physics by the method of the inverse scattering problem. I |journal=Functional Analysis and Its Applications |volume=8 |issue=3 |pages=226–235}}</ref>

In 2002, the regularized version of the KP equation, naturally referred to as the [[Brooke Benjamin|Benjamin]]–[[Jerry L. Bona|Bona]]–[[John Joseph Mahony|Mahony]]–[[Boris Kadomtsev|Kadomtsev]]–[[Vladimir Iosifovich Petviashvili|Petviashvili]] equation (or simply the '''BBM-KP equation'''), was introduced as an alternative model for small amplitude long waves in shallow water moving mainly in the ''x'' direction in 2+1 space.<ref>{{cite journal |first1= J. L.|last1= Bona | author-link1=Jerry L. Bona | first2=Y.|last2= Liu | first3=M. M.|last3= Tom| year=2002 |title=The Cauchy problem and stability of solitary-wave solutions for RLW-KP-type equations |journal=Journal of Differential Equations |volume=185 |issue=2 |pages=437–482 |doi=10.1006/jdeq.2002.4171|bibcode= 2002JDE...185..437B |doi-access=free }}</ref>

:<math>\displaystyle \partial_x(\partial_t u+u \partial_x u+\epsilon^2\partial_{xxt}u)+\lambda\partial_{yy}u=0</math>
where <math>\lambda=\pm 1</math>. The BBM-KP equation provides an alternative to the usual KP equation, in a similar way that the [[Benjamin–Bona–Mahony equation]] is related to the classical [[Korteweg–de Vries equation]], as the linearized dispersion relation of the BBM-KP is a good approximation to that of the KP but does not exhibit the unwanted limiting behavior as the [[Fourier Analysis|Fourier]] variable dual to ''x'' approaches <math>\pm \infty</math>. The BBM-KP equation can be viewed as a weak transverse perturbation of the [[Benjamin–Bona–Mahony equation]]. As a result, the solutions of their corresponding Cauchy problems share an intriguing and complex mathematical relationship. Aguilar et al. proved that the solution of the Cauchy problem for the BBM-KP model equation converges to the solution of the Cauchy problem associated to the [[Benjamin–Bona–Mahony equation]] in the <math>L^2</math> -based [[Sobolev space]] <math>H^{k}_{x}(\R)</math> for all <math> k \ge 1</math>, provided their corresponding initial data are close in <math>H^{k}_{x}(\R)</math> as the transverse variable <math>y \rightarrow \pm \infty</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |first1= J. B.|last1= Aguilar | first2=M.M.|last2= Tom | year=2024 |title=Convergence of solutions of the BBM and BBM-KP model equations
 |journal=Differential and Integral Equations |volume=37 |issue=3/4 |pages=187–206|doi=10.57262/die037-0304-187| doi-access=free |arxiv=2204.06016 }}</ref>

==History==

[[File:RIAN archive 151311 Russian physicist Boris Kadomtsev.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Boris Kadomtsev.]]
The KP equation was first written in 1970 by Soviet physicists Boris B. Kadomtsev (1928–1998) and Vladimir I. Petviashvili (1936–1993); it came as a natural generalization of the KdV equation (derived by Korteweg and De Vries in 1895).  Whereas in the KdV equation waves are strictly one-dimensional, in the KP equation this restriction is relaxed. Still, both in the KdV and the KP equation, waves have to travel in the positive ''x''-direction.

==Connections to physics==

The KP equation can be used to model [[water wave]]s of long [[wavelength]] with weakly non-linear restoring forces and [[dispersion (water waves)|frequency dispersion]].  If [[surface tension]] is weak compared to [[Earth's gravity|gravitational forces]], <math>\lambda=+1</math> is used; if surface tension is strong, then <math>\lambda=-1</math>.  Because of the asymmetry in the way ''x''- and ''y''-terms enter the equation, the waves described by the KP equation behave differently in the direction of propagation (''x''-direction) and transverse (''y'') direction; oscillations in the ''y''-direction tend to be smoother (be of small-deviation).

The KP equation can also be used to model waves in [[Ferromagnetism|ferromagnetic]] media,<ref>{{cite journal |last=Leblond |first=H. |year=2002 |title=KP lumps in ferromagnets: a three-dimensional KdV–Burgers model |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General |volume=35 |issue=47 |pages=10149–10161 |doi=10.1088/0305-4470/35/47/313 |bibcode=2002JPhA...3510149L }}</ref> as well as two-dimensional matter–wave pulses in [[Bose–Einstein condensate]]s.

==Limiting behavior==

For <math>\epsilon\ll 1</math>, typical ''x''-dependent oscillations have a wavelength of <math>O(1/\epsilon)</math> giving a singular limiting regime as <math>\epsilon\rightarrow 0</math>.  The limit <math>\epsilon\rightarrow 0</math> is called the [[Dispersionless equation|dispersion]]less limit.<ref>{{cite book |last=Zakharov |first=V. E. |author-link1=Vladimir E. Zakharov |year=1994 |chapter=Dispersionless limit of integrable systems in 2+1 dimensions |title=Singular limits of dispersive waves |pages=165–174 |publisher=Springer |location=Boston |isbn=0-306-44628-6 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Strachan |first=I. A. |year=1995 |title=The Moyal bracket and the dispersionless limit of the KP hierarchy |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General |volume=28 |issue=7 |page=1967 |doi=10.1088/0305-4470/28/7/018 |arxiv=hep-th/9410048 |bibcode=1995JPhA...28.1967S |s2cid=15334780 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Takasaki |first1=K. |last2=Takebe |first2=T. |year=1995 |title=Integrable hierarchies and dispersionless limit |journal=Reviews in Mathematical Physics |volume=7 |issue=5 |pages=743–808 |doi=10.1142/S0129055X9500030X |arxiv=hep-th/9405096 |bibcode=1995RvMaP...7..743T |s2cid=17351327 }}</ref>

If we also assume that the solutions are independent of ''y'' as <math>\epsilon\rightarrow 0</math>, then they also satisfy the inviscid [[Burgers' equation]]:
:<math>\displaystyle \partial_t u+u\partial_x u=0.</math>

Suppose the amplitude of oscillations of a solution is asymptotically small — <math>O(\epsilon)</math> — in the dispersionless limit. Then the amplitude satisfies a mean-field equation of [[Davey–Stewartson equations|Davey–Stewartson]] type.
